reason: The conclusion STAYS CLOSED holds, but runtime is not what keeps it closed. (1) is correct. V5 says one hidden run covers public and private. #37 and #38 have already scored. K2 is clean (L_hi 7.54 h <= 8.0 h), so the V3/W4 trigger never fired. Headroom is therefore worth 0 for the finals, and I-235 K2'' plus the H1/L2/D4 deadline moves (I-007/I-008/I-009) are moot. (2) is internally inconsistent. It says the binding limit for a new K2-based file is the 8.0 h insertion gate, and also that such a file would need K2''-style deadlines. With those deadlines (DIVINS 32400 = 9.0 h, REPAIR 37800 = 10.5 h), the gate is 9.0 h and the slack is >= 1.46 h. That covers H2's +0.38 h plus the 0.58 h GPU spread. Also, 'slack >= 0.46 h < 0.58 h' compares a lower bound (L includes queue time) with a spread, so it proves nothing. A twin-based file (L_hi 6.87 h, 9.5 h repair) has even more room. The real reasons these ideas stay closed are value, gate and schedule. H2's value lens gives +0.0003 central (refuted). I-144 gives +0.0002. I-156: detector-blend perturbations went 4/4 negative on our LB. The detection-map class went 0/5 on the LB, and the honest-LOEO gains of axis-flip and z-flip turned negative on the LB. The R4 +0.002 public read is unreachable (2-run SD ~0.003). H2 depends on tempfuse, which is unbuilt, and it breaks the pre-registered K2 dummy gates (LOWDET N, raw nodes 121,777). R8 cuts off new mechanisms at 27 Sep 12:00 UTC.
